faq.question: Does this converter create a real XML document?
faq.answer: It generates XML markup with nested elements and escaped text values. Whether the result is accepted by a particular application depends on that application's schema, required namespaces, attributes, element names, ordering, and validation rules.

faq.question: How are JSON objects converted to XML?
faq.answer: JSON object properties are normally converted into nested XML elements. For example, {"user":{"name":"Alice"}} may become <user><name>Alice</name></user>.

faq.question: How are JSON arrays converted to XML?
faq.answer: JSON arrays are commonly represented as repeated XML elements. Because JSON arrays do not define an XML element name, the converter should use a configured array item name or another documented naming rule.

faq.question: Can I customize the root element?
faq.answer: Yes. Enter a valid XML element name for the document root. The default may be root, but you can change it to match the vocabulary expected by your target system.

faq.question: Can I customize the array item element name?
faq.answer: If the option is available, yes. This is useful when an array such as products must become repeated <product> elements rather than generic <item> elements. The correct name depends on the target XML schema.

faq.question: Does JSON to XML conversion preserve data types?
faq.answer: Not completely. XML element content is text unless a schema or application-specific convention provides type information. Numbers, booleans, and null values may therefore need interpretation by the receiving application.

faq.question: Can JSON properties become XML attributes?
faq.answer: Not automatically in a generic JSON-to-XML mapping unless the converter provides an attribute convention or explicit mapping options. JSON has no native attribute concept, so XML attributes require a documented convention such as a reserved key or mapping rule.

faq.question: What happens to null values?
faq.answer: Null values may become empty elements, omitted properties, or an implementation-specific representation. Review the output and confirm the behavior expected by the target XML system.

faq.question: What happens to JSON keys with special characters?
faq.answer: JSON keys used as XML element names must comply with XML naming rules. Keys containing spaces, punctuation, leading digits, or namespace-sensitive characters may need to be sanitized, rejected, or mapped to valid names. Review the output when keys are not conventional identifiers.

faq.question: Are special characters in JSON values escaped?
faq.answer: Text values should be XML-escaped so characters such as ampersands, less-than signs, greater-than signs, and quotation marks do not create invalid markup. Escaping a value does not make an invalid element name valid.

faq.question: Can I use the output for SOAP?
faq.answer: The generated XML may be useful as a payload fragment or starting point, but a SOAP request also requires the correct envelope, namespaces, operation structure, headers, authentication, and service-specific schema. JSON-to-XML conversion alone does not create a complete valid SOAP request.

faq.question: Can I convert XML back to JSON?
faq.answer: Use an XML to JSON converter for the reverse direction. The round trip may not reproduce the original data exactly because XML attributes, namespaces, ordering, mixed content, and schema types do not have direct equivalents in ordinary JSON.

faq.question: Can I convert a large JSON file?
faq.answer: The practical limit depends on browser memory, device performance, document depth, number of elements, and PDF or text generation requirements. Large inputs may take longer to parse and generate.

faq.question: Is my JSON uploaded to a server?
faq.answer: This page is designed to parse JSON and generate XML in your browser without requiring a server upload. You should still avoid entering passwords, API keys, access tokens, private customer data, or confidential production data into any browser-based tool.

faq.question: Is this a free JSON to XML converter?
faq.answer: Yes. You can paste or open JSON, configure the available XML options, and copy or download the output without creating an account.

article.title: How to Convert JSON to XML Online
article.content:
What Is a JSON to XML Converter?

A JSON to XML converter maps JSON objects, arrays, and scalar values to XML elements and text content. This can help when a modern JSON workflow needs to communicate with an older integration, XML-based configuration system, document format, or service that expects XML.

JSON and XML are different data models. JSON has objects and arrays, while XML has elements, attributes, namespaces, text nodes, mixed content, and document-level declarations. A conversion therefore follows a set of mapping rules rather than performing a perfectly lossless format swap.

Common Use Cases

  • Legacy integration: Prepare JSON data for a system that accepts XML rather than JSON.
  • API and service testing: Convert sample JSON into XML for testing an XML endpoint or integration boundary.
  • Configuration conversion: Create an XML representation for a tool that expects XML configuration.
  • Documentation: Show the XML form of an example JSON object when documenting a data mapping.
  • Data migration: Transform structured JSON into an XML starting point for a migration or import workflow.

How to Convert JSON to XML

  1. Enter JSON: Paste a valid JSON object, array, or supported scalar value.
  2. Choose a root element: Set a valid XML root name that matches the target document or schema.
  3. Choose array item names: If the input contains arrays, define the element name used for repeated items where supported.
  4. Configure formatting: Choose indentation and decide whether to include the XML declaration.
  5. Convert: Generate the XML and review the output for valid names, escaped text, null values, and repeated elements.
  6. Copy or download: Copy the XML or save it as a .xml file for testing or integration.

How JSON Structures Map to XML

  • Objects: Object properties become nested XML elements.
  • Arrays: Array values are commonly represented by repeated sibling elements.
  • Strings: Strings become XML text content after special characters are escaped.
  • Numbers and booleans: Values become text, so the receiving system must interpret their types or apply an XML schema.
  • Null: Null may become an empty element, be omitted, or use a documented convention.

Arrays Need an XML Naming Rule

JSON arrays contain values but do not assign an element name to each item. XML requires element names, so a converter must choose a rule. For example:

{"products":[{"name":"Laptop"},{"name":"Mouse"}]}

may become:

<products>
  <product>
    <name>Laptop</name>
  </product>
  <product>
    <name>Mouse</name>
  </product>
</products>

Some converters use item, some derive a singular form such as product, and others allow an explicit item name. If the output must satisfy an XSD or API schema, configure the array item name deliberately.

XML Element Names and Escaping

JSON keys become XML element names only when they follow XML naming rules. Keys containing spaces, invalid punctuation, or leading digits may need sanitization or may produce a conversion error. Text values have a separate requirement: characters such as &, <, and > must be escaped so they do not break the XML document.

Escaping text values does not solve invalid tag names. If the source JSON contains arbitrary user-generated keys, review or map those keys before relying on the XML output.

XML Declaration and Encoding

An XML declaration can identify the document version and declared encoding:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>

The declared encoding should match the actual bytes in the downloaded file. A text string displayed in a browser may be Unicode, while a downloaded file can use a different encoding depending on the implementation. Do not let users select an encoding label that the exporter does not actually produce.

Attributes and JSON

JSON does not have a built-in attribute type. A generic converter therefore usually represents JSON properties as XML elements rather than attributes. If a target system requires attributes, use an explicit mapping convention, such as reserved keys or a field-mapping configuration, and validate the output against the target schema.

JSON to XML and SOAP

XML can be used by SOAP services, but converting JSON into XML does not automatically create a valid SOAP request. SOAP also requires an envelope, namespaces, an operation-specific body, headers, authentication, and a service-defined schema. Use the generated XML as a payload or mapping reference only after checking the service documentation.

JSON to XML Is Not Always Reversible

Converting JSON to XML and then back to JSON may change the data shape. XML introduces attributes, namespaces, ordering, text nodes, and mixed content, while JSON distinguishes arrays and objects differently. Keep the original JSON and validate the generated XML when exact data preservation matters.

Validation and Common Problems

  • Invalid JSON: Missing commas, unmatched braces, invalid quotes, and trailing commas can prevent conversion.
  • Invalid root name: The root element must follow XML naming rules.
  • Ambiguous arrays: The generated repeated element name may not match the target schema.
  • Null handling: Empty or omitted values may not be interpreted the same way by every receiving system.
  • Attributes missing: Generic JSON-to-XML conversion usually creates elements, not XML attributes.
  • Schema mismatch: Well-formed XML can still fail validation against an XSD or service-specific schema.

Browser-Based Privacy

This converter is designed to parse JSON and generate XML in the browser instead of sending the source data to a remote conversion service. That is convenient for one-off transformations and integration tests, but it is not a replacement for secure secret management. Avoid entering credentials, access tokens, private customer information, or production secrets into any web-based tool.

When to Use a Local or Schema-Aware Converter

A browser tool is suitable for quick transformations and inspection. Use a local library, command-line tool, or schema-aware integration workflow for repeatable automation, confidential data, large files, strict XSD validation, namespaces, SOAP envelopes, or precise attribute mappings.

article.title: 如何在线将 JSON 转换为 XML
article.content:
为什么要将 JSON 转换为 XML？

虽然 JSON 是现代 Web API 的主流格式，但 XML 仍然广泛用于企业系统、SOAP Web 服务和遗留应用程序。将 JSON 转换为 XML 可以让你将基于 JSON 的现代服务与现有的 XML 基础设施集成。

常见使用场景

  • 企业集成：将现代 REST API 与基于 XML 的传统企业系统连接
  • SOAP Web 服务：将 JSON 负载转换为 SOAP 端点所需的 XML 格式
  • 配置文件：将 JSON 配置转换为 XML 格式，供期望 XML 配置的系统使用
  • 数据交换：与使用 XML 作为标准交换格式的合作伙伴或系统共享数据
  • 迁移项目：在基于 JSON 的存储和基于 XML 的归档之间迁移数据

JSON 与 XML 的对比

  • JSON：轻量级、简洁、易读，对 JavaScript 环境原生友好
  • XML：更冗长，支持属性和命名空间，并有成熟的 schema 验证工具（XSD）

由于其简单性，JSON 通常是新 Web API 的首选，但在许多企业和受监管的环境中，XML 仍然非常重要。

如何将 JSON 转换为 XML

  1. 粘贴 JSON：在输入框中添加 JSON 对象或数组。
  2. 设置根元素：可选地指定自定义根元素名称（默认：root）。
  3. 配置选项：选择缩进（2 或 4 空格）和 XML 编码，以匹配你的需求。
  4. 点击转换：将 JSON 转换为格式良好的 XML 文档。
  5. 复制或下载：将 XML 复制到剪贴板，或保存为 .xml 文件，用于集成工作流。

JSON 结构如何映射到 XML

  • 对象：变成嵌套的 XML 元素，保留层级关系。
  • 数组：转换为在父节点下重复出现的同名元素。
  • 基本类型值：字符串、数字和布尔值成为 XML 元素的文本内容。
  • Null 值：可能表示为空元素或被省略，具体取决于转换策略。

最佳实践

  • 选择好的根名称：使用能反映数据用途的描述性元素名称。
  • 验证输出：检查生成的 XML 是否格式良好，如有需要，可针对 XSD schema 进行验证。
  • 考虑属性：JSON 没有属性概念，所有数据都会变成元素。如果目标系统期望属性，可能需要进行后处理。
  • 处理特殊字符：检查带有特殊字符的键如何被转换，确保生成有效的 XML 标签。
  • 保留备份：保留原始 JSON，以便在需要用不同选项重新生成 XML 时使用。

浏览器本地处理与隐私

这个 JSON 转 XML 转换器在浏览器中处理输入内容，不要求将数据上传到远程服务。对于开发数据和私密配置片段来说，本地处理更加方便。不过，仍然不建议在任何浏览器工具中输入密码、API 密钥、访问令牌或其他高度敏感的信息。
